key_facts: The baseline system achieved 82% accuracy on the Italian mismatched digits task.
The multi-English training set with PLP and delta features achieved 89.7% accuracy on the Italian mismatched digits task.
Using on-line normalization and a neural network improved accuracy to nearly 90% for the Italian mismatched digits task.
The PLP features performed similarly to mel cepstra features in terms of accuracy.
The MSG features did not significantly improve accuracy when combined with PLP features for the Italian mismatched digits task.
The TIMIT training set, which is hand-labeled, produced the best results among the training sets.
The use of delta features was found to be important for improving accuracy.
The researchers are considering using multi-band features and integrating neural networks into existing systems.
There are ongoing experiments with different training sets and feature combinations to determine the best approach for improving accuracy.
The researchers are planning to test the effectiveness of combining features and neural network outputs across various test sets.
The researchers are exploring the use of different training targets, including articulatory and soft targets, to reduce language dependency.
The researchers are addressing CPU and memory constraints in their experiments.
The researchers are working on integrating their neural network system with the OGI system.
The researchers are considering the use of variance scaling techniques to adjust the contribution of different feature streams.
The researchers are planning to evaluate the performance of their system across a range of different test conditions, including various languages and noise types.
